prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: King battle faceplate variant; edit the supplied accepted head sheet, keep the original two-view layout and actual transparent alpha.
Primary request: Create a DEPLOYABLE BATTLE MASK for this exact King head. The supplied source is the approved NORMAL FACE. This must look like the SAME head putting on its own protective mouth/nose armor, comparable to the familiar Orion Pax / Optimus Prime normal-face versus battle-mask contrast. Do not draw Optimus Prime or replace King's design.
Change ONLY lower face armor in BOTH views, consistently. Preserve absolutely the accepted FIVE crown components, single forward/up curving central blade horn with small backward notch, two long inner and two short outer antennas, navy dome proportions, eye shape and pale warm eye color, brow, forehead, round gold ear housings, gold cheek frames, neck and camera. Front head remains exactly symmetric. Do not flatten head or elongate crown.
Battle mask design: two mirror-image IVORY faceted armor half-plates deploy from recessed pockets behind the existing cheek frames, rotate forward and meet at the facial centerline. Closed they form one broad, strong angular respirator shield over the nose and mouth down to the jaw, slightly projecting forward from the normal face. A crisp narrow vertical center seam and raised beveled median ridge clearly show the two-piece construction. At each side, one small inset navy stepped vent with subtle gold edge ties the mask to King's cheek/chest armor language; keep the center broad and clean. Navy border at lower mask rim; thin restrained gold joint/edge details, not a full gold face. A small portion of the established crimson CHIN TAB remains visible below the mask as a locking latch.
The normal mouth and nose opening are HIDDEN, no lips, no drawn mouth-line on the mask; do not merely erase the old mouth line. The top mask edge fits beneath the eyes, and the faceplate projects noticeably in side profile with visible armor thickness and a small hinge/slide root at the cheek. The eyes and eyebrows remain fully exposed, readable and unchanged. No new visor over eyes.
Side profile shows the SAME mask, not a different single-piece face: the near half's angular front cover, center join at the front, and its connection to the existing cheek pocket. Plate panels do not grow from the neck or forehead. Preserve royal/heavy armored identity.
Composition: identical front-left and left-profile-right sheet, complete horn tips and collars. No extra inset, no arrows, no captions, no symbols, no text. Clean crisp cel-shaded mecha illustration consistent with the input; true transparent background. No other changes.

Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: visual mechanism sequence for King's retractable battle mask, horizontal THREE-FRAME lower-face detail sheet on genuine transparent alpha, clean cel mecha concept art.
Input image 1: authority for NORMAL King face, use the LEFT FRONT view. Input image 2: exact newly designed CLOSED BATTLE MASK, use its LEFT FRONT view. Keep this single robot's identity and plate design; do not invent another head.
Show three equal FRONT VIEW detail crops of the SAME head at the SAME scale, aligned brow/eye line and chin, left to right. Crop intentionally just above the eyebrow crown band and below the neck collar, so this is a face-mechanism detail and the tall crown tips are outside the framing in all three panels. Keep eyes, round gold ear housings, gold cheek frames, navy side helmet and red chin latch identical across all stages. No unrelated body.
Frame 1 NORMAL / STOWED: the exact bare ivory face, visible normal navy nose and subtle mouth line from image 1. Two mask halves are folded/retracted out of sight in recessed pockets behind the gold cheek frames. Do not add new exposed mouth armor in this stage.
Frame 2 DEPLOYING: the SAME normal face remains behind, still visible through a wide center gap. Exactly TWO ivory mask half-plates, matching the LEFT HALF and RIGHT HALF of the final mask in image 2, have slid FORWARD from pockets behind the stationary cheek frames. They are slightly swung outward on SHORT DARK MECHANICAL LINK ARMS, ONE arm per side, connected to the inner cheek structure, then moving inward toward the face center. These are two half-masks, not two copies of an entire mask. Their inner vertical join edges are clearly separate and approaching each other. Show enough connection and thickness to understand the source of the panels. The mask plates remain attached to the cheeks; they never float, grow from the face or come from the neck. Add two small flat gold/orange motion arrows pointing inward, off the eye line.
Frame 3 CLOSED: the exact closed mask from image 2. Two matching ivory faceted halves meet along ONE narrow vertical center seam and raised bevel ridge, cover normal nose and mouth, with navy side vents and gold/blue border. Small red chin locking tab remains visible below. The width, height, facet outlines and color of these two deployed halves MUST match Frame 2.
Use two simple small rightward progression arrows in the gaps BETWEEN the frames. No words, no letters, no numbering, no watermark. Strong mechanical continuity, clean readable diagram, no new fins, no floating extra parts, no eye visor. The main task is the believable source and route of the same two mask halves. Do not claim engineering-exact kinematics. Genuine transparent background.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target Image 1 is King's current APPROVED BATTLE-MASK head sheet, FRONT at left and LEFT SIDE PROFILE facing screen-left at right. Supporting Image 2 is the user's red outline annotation of the SIDE PROFILE, indicating the ADDITIONAL RED MIDLINE HELMET FIN. Red drawing marks are placement/design instructions, not surface graphics.
Primary request: Add exactly ONE CRIMSON-RED DORSAL FIN to the sagittal CENTERLINE of the helmet top, BEHIND the existing gold forehead horn. Nothing else changes. Keep the battle mask exactly as it is; the user approved it.
Fin geometry: a thin flat fore-aft blade set vertically on the helmet's middle ridge, its wide triangular side face clearly seen in LEFT PROFILE, rooted along the navy helmet dome from behind the gold forehead mounting to the rear crown. The front fin edge rises obliquely toward a high rearward peak, then its back edge slopes down to the back of the helmet, roughly following the user's marked triangular outline. Use a strong tapered streamlined dorsal crest, crimson main face, darker red rear facet and a narrow brighter red bevel. Its apex sits above the rear dome around the upper inner gold-antenna zone, but BELOW the extreme tip of the long gold central horn. It is an integrated helmet crest, not a huge axe, sail, plume, loose spike or separate side antenna. Thin construction with a narrow navy mounting root.
Projection is essential: this red fin is on the helmet midline, NOT on the visible temple or either ear. In FRONT view its broad side face is edge-on and largely occluded by the center gold horn; only a naturally visible THIN red center edge / small rear tip is allowed if it is not hidden by the horn. Do not invent a wide red triangle, extra red horns, or move the gold horn sideways just to expose it. Preserve correct occlusion. In SIDE view show the red triangular fin seated behind the gold crown and in front of the rear dome silhouette as annotated.
Invariants: keep exact same accepted gold five-member crown: one thick upward curving central horn with rear notch, TWO long inner fins, TWO shorter outer fins. Keep every gold antenna's shape, direction, scale and root. Keep navy shell height, eye shape/color, gold brow and round ears, gold cheek vents, the broad ivory TWO-HALF BATTLE MASK with center seam, red chin latch, neck, face proportions and camera exactly. No new shoulder/body, no flattening head. Do not recolor the accepted gold horns to red.
Keep original two-view composition, complete tips, transparent alpha, clean cel linework and shading. No text, no arrows, no sketches, no visible red annotation strokes.

jobs.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct ONLY the red fin's FRONT-VIEW PROJECTION in the LEFT head. Preserve the entire RIGHT SIDE PROFILE including its broad triangular crimson dorsal fin exactly. This is one thin flat fin on the sagittal midline, directly BEHIND the broad gold center horn and SHORTER than that gold horn. Therefore in strict FRONT view the red fin is COMPLETELY OCCLUDED by the gold horn, not visible as a triangular red backing or two red stripes. Remove ONLY the two exposed red side slivers behind the upper center gold horn in the left head; restore underlying navy/transparent areas naturally. Keep all gold edges, all five gold antennas, their dimensions, helmet dome, faceplate, eyes, cheek vents, red chin tab, neck, camera, composition and alpha exactly unchanged. Do not remove or change any part of the side-profile red fin. No other changes. No letters, no arrows, no extra objects.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the edit target: King's NEW helmet with one crimson midline dorsal fin and closed battle mask, front-left and left-profile-right sheet. Image 2 is the authority for the original NORMAL FACE only.
Create the NORMAL FACE state of exactly the Image 1 helmet: retract/remove ONLY the two ivory battle-mask cover halves and restore the original normal navy nose bridge, ivory angular face, subtle mouth line, heavy jaw and crimson chin from Image 2, in both views. Keep exact same helmet dome, gold crown with FIVE members, eyes, ears, cheek frames, and especially the side-profile triangular crimson top fin from Image 1 completely unchanged. Do not remove the new red fin when the mask retracts. Keep head scale/camera/collar fixed, no flattened skull.
One additional projection correction is REQUIRED in the left FRONT head: this red fin is a thin sagittal blade directly BEHIND and SHORTER than the broad gold center horn, so it is completely occluded in strict front view. Remove the two incorrectly exposed red slivers beside that upper center gold horn; retain the SIDE PROFILE red fin exactly. Do not make two red horns or shift the gold horn aside.
The same helmet and fin must work for normal and battle states; only lower face coverage changes. No labels, no arrows, no extra heads or insets. Preserve genuine transparent background and existing cel drawing style.
